title: jövő héten: The Same Choice, at a Week's Scale

sections.title: One time word, still two constructions
sections.content: jövő héten works exactly like holnap did: it doesn't decide for you whether to use the present tense or fog + infinitive. A regular, already-fixed part of your week still takes the present tense you already know. A prediction, an intention, or something depending on how the week goes reaches for fog + infinitive instead.

items.english: Next week I'm working, like always. (fixed routine)

items.spanish: Jövő héten valószínűleg sokat fogunk telefonálni Ildikónak.
items.english: Next week we'll probably call Ildikó a lot. (a prediction, not yet fixed)

items.spanish: Petra jövő héten megbeszéli a projektet a főnökével.
items.english: Petra is discussing the project with her boss next week. (already arranged)

items.spanish: A csapat biztosan fog dolgozni a projekten.
items.english: The team will definitely work on the project. (a promise about how things will go)

sections.content: A useful test: could you write this straight into your calendar as a fact? If yes, present tense. If it's really a guess about how the week will turn out, fog + infinitive fits better — even with the exact same time word in front of it.
